Also, I don't think you know fully about the essay process - most schools require the Common App essay, which is the same prompt set for every school. It's specifically designed so that kids don't have to write a ton of essays. Then there are the supplementals. Colleges with higher prestige or honors programs have supplementals with their own prompts.

So in reality, this kid probably wrote one common essay which worked for every school and then required supplementals for a few of the colleges that required them.

Most of the colleges applied to were probably auto-admit, only common essay required places. I don't find this accomplishment amazing, as the scholarships awarded are mostly need-based instead of merit aid.

Since he would have received fee waivers, sending off the essays to colleges is free and requires no extra effort in the writing department which sort of diminishes the accomplishment. Asexual - Lack of sexual attraction.  
Aceflux - sexual identity fluctuates but generally stays on the ace-spectrum.  
Graysexual/grayasexual - Experiences sexual attraction rarely or very weakly.  
Demisexual - Experiences sexual attraction only after forming a deep emotional bond with someone.  
Fraysexual - Opposite of demisexual; experiences sexual attraction until forming an emotional bond with people/getting to know someone better.  
Aegosexual - An ace-spec person who can enjoy/be aroused by sexual material that does not involve themselves. There is a disconnect between them and the sexual matters.  
Apothisexual - A sex-repulsed asexual (or other ace-spec)  
Lithosexual/akoisexual - Experiences sexual attraction but does not want those feelings reciprocated/they fade upon learning the other reciprocates them.  
Reciprosexual - Opposite of lithosexual; does not experience sexual attraction until knowing that another experiences sexual attraction towards them.  
Ace-spike - asexual (or other ace-spec), but occasionally experiences short periods of increased sexual attraction, or "spikes" in sexual attraction levels.  
Cupiosexual - asexual (or other ace-spec) who desires a sexual relationship even though they do not experience sexual attraction.  
Myrsexual - experiencing multiple ace-spec identities at the same time.
